title: Every brush follows the pointer with no lag, even at 150 pt and up
goal: The brushes look good but feel laggy to use: watercolour and oil clearly trail the pointer at 150 pt or more, and the user finds brushes laggy in general. Every brush, at every size, should keep up with the hand with no visible delay, without changing how it looks.
notes: User, 2026-10-25: 'the watercolor looks good but it's slow if i increase the size to 150pt or more, feels quite laggy', then 'actually so does oil... still trying everything but the brushes feel very laggy to use'. A cause shared by every medium (the live overlay, CanvasBrush.swift) is as likely as per-medium cost. Not reproduced in the intake window. Theories only: Sources/PhotonzRender/Watercolour.swift mark(_:) walks every pixel of a box radius*(1+farthest) around each dab on the CPU, so the work grows with the square of the size and with how close dabs are spaced; reach() loops over every earlier wet wash per pixel; WetField.ensure copies the whole field when it grows; and the live stroke (Sources/Photonz/CanvasBrush.swift) may be building a full CGImage of the overlay per drag. Measure which of these it actually is before fixing.
acceptance: Reproduce first and MEASURE, for every brush medium (watercolour, oil, charcoal, chalk, pencil, marker, crayon, airbrush, plain): time per drag event and the lag from pointer to painted dab at 20, 50, 150, 300 and 500 pt on a Retina canvas, in the probe at Next defaults, written in the audit as a table before any change. The 150 pt numbers for watercolour and oil have to show the lag the user felt, or the task says what else it is (for example the canvas redraw or the overlay, not the medium).

After the fix, every drag event at 150 to 500 pt finishes inside one 120 Hz frame (8 ms) at p95 and the painted dab never trails the pointer by more than one frame, MEASURED with the same harness and put in the audit beside the before numbers.

The look does not change: the finished stroke at 150 and 300 pt matches today's pixel for pixel or within a measured tolerance the audit states (bloom, fingers, edge darkening and the bleed into earlier wet washes all still there), with before and after pictures.

Every medium meets the 8 ms p95 bar at every measured size, including small sizes (the user called brushes laggy in general, not only big ones); the table in the audit shows before and after for all of them.
Rendering changes carry the perf note the repo asks for. Logic in PhotonzRender is test-first.
Try path: Next defaults, Brush tool, for watercolour and oil at 200 pt and every other medium at 50 pt, scribble fast across the canvas; the paint keeps up with the pointer.
An audit under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.
Measured on a 12 megapixel canvas whose paint layer already holds 50 strokes (moved from painting-is-what-you-see-earlier-strokes-never-r on 2026-10-28), as well as on an empty layer

log.note: Related user ask filed 2026-10-25: painting-is-what-you-see-earlier-strokes-never-r (earlier strokes re-simulated and swapped to a sharper copy on every new stroke; paint-layer raster cache keyed by the whole content). Likely the same root; do not fix it two different ways.

From the smudge freeze task (2026-10-25): a paint layer now keeps its last raster (PaintRasterCache in PhotonzRender) and a brush press reads the paint under it ready-drawn in the background (CanvasNSView.warmBrushPaint), so oil and watercolour presses no longer re-simulate the layer: 190-461 ms down to 0.1 ms on a 12 MP canvas. Still left for this task: a watercolour press into a wash still wet holds the main thread 90-100 ms replaying the wet washes in view pixels (WetWashes.under in LiveMarker.init), and watercolour moves reach 7-10 ms p95 (smudge-after-paint-keeps-up-walk drag lines).

User, 2026-10-25 (after the smudge fix d2efecfb landed): 'brushes are slow. at first its fine, after 3 or 4 large strokes it gets progressively worse perf. it needs to be constant and fast'. So the cost per drag GROWS with the number of strokes already on the layer. The bar for this task: per-drag time at stroke 1, 5, 10 and 50 (large brush) is MEASURED and stays flat, the 50th no slower than the 1st beyond noise, as well as inside the 8 ms p95. Suspects to measure, not assume: the live stroke reading every earlier wet wash (Watercolour under()/WetWash per pixel), a whole-layer re-rasterize per stroke, the overlay bitmap growing.

triage 2026-10-28, folded from painting-is-what-you-see-earlier-strokes-never-r: its 2026-10-27 pass took 500 pt oil from 20.2 to 15.3 ms p95 (charcoal 16.5 to 14.7, pencil 13.8 to 12.6, watercolour 14.1, marker 7.8; 150 pt 10.4 to 11.4; 20 pt 2.5 to 4.3) on 12 MP with 50 strokes. Profile of 500 pt oil on the main thread: the parallel pixel loop of lay() about 65%, field growth (mostly the tail journal saving its boxes) about 14%, the serial per-bristle sum about 10%, 6 MB of scratch allocated and zeroed per dab about 7%. Per move: settled dab about 5 ms, tail re-laid about 4.5, take-back about 2.5, redraw about 1, screen hand-off about 1. 12 bands instead of 8 did not help. Next levers named there: reuse the dab scratch, save the tail journal once per move over the union rather than per dab and field, skip rows and columns outside the rotated footprint. Reaching 8.3 ms at 500 pt may need a cheaper oil or dry model, which would change how saved strokes paint: that is a card for the user, not a quiet change

From painting-is-what-you-see (2026-10-30): measured against the code before the WYSIWYG change, 150 pt oil, pencil, charcoal and marker got 2-3x slower per move (screenshot at fit: oil 4.5->11.3 ms p95, pencil 3.1->10.1), 500 pt got quicker. Half of a 150 pt oil move is laying the live thinned end again (4 dabs a move). Tables, profile and both walks: queue/audits/2026-10-30-paint-move-cost.txt. Getting under 8 ms here likely closes that task's last item too.

From painting-is-what-you-see (d233562c, 2026-10-30): dab pixels now split across cores at a far smaller size, pencil/crayon dabs batched, charcoal smear by rows, tail journal saves once, overlay pieces 128 px. 12 MP at fit p95: 150 pt oil 6.4, pencil 4.6, charcoal 5.5, marker 2.9, watercolour 5.1; 500 pt watercolour 13.7, oil 13.5, pencil 11.9, charcoal 13.8, marker 6.1. 1600x1000 at fit, 500 pt: oil 20.8, charcoal 17.4, pencil 16.5. Remaining per-move cost is the dab work itself (oil lay per pixel, dry tip paper/streak reads) times the re-laid tail. Measurement walks: queue/audits/2026-10-30-paint-move-cost-*.walk.

Reproduced and measured (8bc940fb): the lag was mostly the cores slowing between dabs (same 500 pt oil dab 4.8 ms back to back, 10.7 ms with 8 ms gaps). Fixed with a core kept running while painting (CoresReady) plus cheaper oil and dry dabs, same pixels byte for byte (BigBrushKeepsItsPixelsTests). p95 a move, before -> after: every medium at 20/50/150/300/500 pt on 12 MP (50 strokes and empty) now under 8 ms (500 pt worst chalk 14.5 -> 6.7); 50 strokes vs empty layer flat (oil 500 5.0 vs 4.9). Screenshot size (1600x1000 at fit) all under 8 ms except 500 pt: chalk 23.3 -> 12.6, charcoal 20.8 -> 10.2, oil 22.3 -> 9.0, watercolour 16.2 -> 8.2. Tables: queue/audits/2026-10-30-brush-lag-measures.txt; audit 2026-10-30-every-brush-follows-the-pointer-with-no-lag-even.json.

Left open: items 2 and 4 (8 ms at every size) still miss at 500 pt on a screenshot-size canvas for chalk, charcoal, oil (watercolour borderline). Release bench, same case, with the live thinned end off: oil 7.1 -> 4.0, chalk 10.5 -> 6.1, charcoal 8.2 -> 5.3, so the remainder is the end re-laid each move, which the user's pending card on painting-is-what-you-see (option b) decides. Tried and dropped: skipping dry pixels a dab could not raise (streaks keep the bound too high, no gain). Six brush walks fail at the brush chooser; all were already failing in the last sweep and are owned by walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep-26, not this change.
Most of the bar reached (8bc940fb): every size on 12 MP and up to 300 pt on a screenshot under 8 ms; 500 pt chalk, charcoal and oil on a screenshot still 9 to 12.6 ms, waiting on the thinned-end card
